ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/writing-skills/references/flowcharts.md` for when a flowchart is warranted, the graphviz style rules, and the render tool.

ACTION: Read `specs/cache-invalidation-baseline.md` to get the reasons the agents gave for purging in the 11 failing runs. The decision nodes need to test the predicates those reps got wrong.

ACTION: Read `skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md` to see the current purge-versus-expire guidance, so the flowchart replaces or sits next to it without contradicting it.

I'm reading three files before I edit anything: the flowchart style rules, the baseline reasons, and the current SKILL.md. I don't have the exact reasons from the 11 purge failures in front of me. I want each decision node to test something an agent can observe, such as "is the stale value harmful to serve until its TTL?", not a judgment call, and the reasons will show which predicates the agents misjudged.

After the reads I'll add the flowchart to `skills/cache-invalidation/SKILL.md` in the style the reference requires, and render it to check it. Then I'll rerun the same three scenarios, 5 reps each, with the updated skill. If the purge rate stays high, I'll tighten the nodes against the new reasons before calling it done.
